entries.label: CO - Certificate of Occupancy
entries.summary: Town sign-off that a home is fit to live in. For a resale, many NJ towns require one. Property Home shows this town's rules, fees and who to call.
entries.where: Property Home > Closing > Town CO & fire certificate

entries.label: CCO - Certificate of Continued Occupancy
entries.summary: A certificate some NJ towns require after a local inspection before a home is sold. Property Home shows this town's rules, fees and who to call.
entries.where: Property Home > Closing > Town CO & fire certificate

entries.label: Smoke, CO alarm and fire extinguisher certificate
entries.summary: NJ requires it before a one- or two-family home is sold or rented. Property Home shows who issues it in this town, the fee and who to call.
entries.where: Property Home > Closing > Town CO & fire certificate

entries.label: Open permits and unpermitted work
entries.summary: Permits that never got a final sign-off, or work done without a permit. Either can hold up a CO, a CCO or the closing.

entries.label: Open code violations
entries.summary: Unresolved town code or housing violations on the property. They often must be cleared or handled before closing.

entries.label: Municipal lien search
entries.summary: A search of town records for unpaid taxes, water and sewer bills and special assessments that must be paid at closing.

entries.label: Property tax status at closing
entries.summary: Confirms the property taxes are paid up to date with the town tax collector before the home closes.

entries.label: Tax sale and tax lien certificates
entries.summary: If taxes stay unpaid, a NJ town can sell a tax lien on the property at a tax sale. The lien must be paid off before closing.

entries.label: Water and sewer final reading
entries.summary: A last meter reading ordered before closing so the seller's water and sewer balance can be paid.

entries.label: Title commitment
entries.summary: The title company's report of what it will insure, what must be cleared first and any exceptions.

entries.label: Mortgage payoff
entries.summary: The exact amount needed to pay off the seller's mortgage or HELOC at closing. Order it early from each lender.

entries.label: Deed and recording
entries.summary: The recorded document that transfers ownership. Check the owner of record and the deed book and page with the county.

entries.label: Judgment and lien search
entries.summary: A search for court judgments and recorded liens against the owners that could attach to the property.

entries.label: Lis pendens
entries.summary: A recorded notice that a lawsuit about the property is pending, such as a foreclosure. Title must clear it before closing.

entries.label: Closing documents
entries.summary: One private file per deal for title, lender, inspection and certificate papers, including CO and CCO copies.

entries.label: Final walk-through
entries.summary: The buyer's last visit before closing to confirm the home's condition and that agreed repairs are done.

entries.label: Attorney review
entries.summary: A 3 business day window after a NJ sales contract is signed when either side's attorney can cancel it or ask for changes.

entries.label: Home inspection
entries.summary: The buyer's inspection of the home's condition. Track the report and any repair requests or credits.

entries.label: Mortgage commitment
entries.summary: The lender's written loan approval, often with conditions that must be met before closing.

entries.label: Private well and septic
entries.summary: Homes on a private well or septic have extra steps. NJ requires a well water test when the home is sold.

entries.label: Oil tank
entries.summary: A buried or unused heating oil tank. Buyers often order a tank sweep, and removal needs a town permit.

entries.label: Solar lease or PPA
entries.summary: Panels may be owned, financed, leased or under a power purchase agreement (PPA). Leases and loans need a transfer or payoff plan.

entries.label: HOA and condo documents
entries.summary: Associations may require a resale package, paid-up dues and approvals before a sale closes.

entries.label: Environmental and deed controls
entries.summary: Public records on contamination, cleanup, deed notices and flood risk that can affect the property or the sale.

entries.label: Municipal services and move-in
entries.summary: Move-in details from the town, such as trash and recycling pickup, for the new owner.

entries.label: Seller disclosures
entries.summary: Seller answers about liens, past work, oil tanks, solar, tenants and more, matched to the closing checklist.

entries.label: Closing readiness checklist
entries.summary: A checklist and score showing how many closing items are resolved for each deal.

entries.label: Client room
entries.summary: A shared page where your buyer or seller can follow milestones and shared documents.

entries.label: Transactions
entries.summary: Track each deal from contract to closing: evidence review, readiness checklist, documents and timeline.

entries.label: Tax checkups for past clients
entries.summary: Send past clients a yearly check on whether their assessment holds up and when they would need to appeal.

entries.label: True Cost Card
entries.summary: A page to share with buyers: the real tax bill, what could change it after the sale and the full monthly cost.
entries.where: Agent Desk > Clients > True Cost Card

entries.label: Property tax appeal
entries.summary: Ask the county tax board to lower your assessment. Usually due April 1 (May 1 in a revaluation year), or January 15 in Burlington, Gloucester and Monmouth.

entries.label: Assessed value
entries.summary: The value your town puts on a property for taxes. Your bill is roughly the assessed value times the local tax rate.

entries.label: Added assessment
entries.summary: An extra tax bill for new construction or improvements finished during the year, prorated for the months after the work is done.

entries.label: Omitted assessment
entries.summary: A tax bill for property or improvements that should have been assessed but were left off the regular tax list.

entries.label: Director's Ratio (equalization ratio)
entries.summary: The state-certified average ratio of assessed value to market value in a town. Used in tax appeals and to split county taxes between towns.

entries.label: Chapter 123
entries.summary: NJ appeal rule that tests an assessment against market value using the town's average ratio and a 15% range.

entries.label: Common level range
entries.summary: The band 15% above and below a town's average ratio. If a home's ratio is above it, the tax board can lower the assessment.

entries.label: COD - Coefficient of Deviation
entries.summary: Measures how evenly a town assesses homes. A lower number means assessments are more uniform.

entries.label: Revaluation vs reassessment
entries.summary: Town-wide resets of assessments to market value. An outside firm usually does a revaluation; the assessor does a reassessment.

entries.label: True value vs assessed value
entries.summary: True value is what a home would likely sell for. Assessed value is the taxable value on the town's tax list.
entries.where: Glossary > True value vs assessed value

entries.label: Effective tax rate
entries.summary: Tax as a share of a home's market value. It makes tax burdens comparable between towns.
entries.where: Glossary > Tax rate vs effective tax rate

entries.label: Tax rate
entries.summary: The yearly rate per $100 of assessed value that pays for town, school and county budgets.

entries.label: ANCHOR Applications
aliases: affordable new jersey communities for homeowners and renters
entries.summary: Prepare your ANCHOR form and track where it stands, then sign and mail it yourself. ANCHOR is NJ's yearly property tax relief for homeowners and renters.

entries.label: Senior Freeze - Property Tax Reimbursement
entries.summary: Pays back eligible seniors and disabled homeowners for property tax increases above their base year amount.

entries.label: PAS-1 - Senior relief application
entries.summary: The single NJ form for people 65 or older, or on Social Security disability, to apply for ANCHOR, Senior Freeze and Stay NJ.

entries.label: Stay NJ - Senior property tax credit
entries.summary: A state credit for eligible homeowners 65 or older that can pay part of the property tax bill, up to a yearly cap.

entries.label: Veterans property tax deduction
entries.summary: A $250 yearly deduction for eligible NJ veterans or surviving spouses. A 100% service-connected disability can mean a full exemption.

entries.label: Senior and disabled person deduction
entries.summary: A $250 yearly deduction for low-income homeowners who are 65 or older or permanently disabled. Apply through your town tax office.

entries.label: Tax abatement vs exemption
entries.summary: An exemption removes value from taxation. An abatement lowers or phases in the tax under a specific program.

entries.label: PILOT - Payment in Lieu of Taxes
entries.summary: A negotiated payment an approved project makes instead of regular property taxes, often under a redevelopment plan.

entries.label: Farmland assessment
entries.summary: A lower assessment for land actively farmed that meets NJ acreage and income rules. A change in use can bring rollback taxes.

entries.label: SR-1A sales record
entries.summary: The state's record of each NJ property sale. The Division of Taxation uses it to compare sale prices with assessments.

entries.label: MOD-IV assessment records
entries.summary: NJ's standard format for town assessment records, including owner, assessed values, property class, block and lot.

entries.label: Block, lot and qualifier
entries.summary: The tax map numbers that identify a NJ parcel. A qualifier marks a unit within a lot, such as a condo.

entries.label: RTF - Realty Transfer Fee
entries.summary: A NJ fee paid when a deed is recorded, based on the sale price. The seller usually pays it; some sellers get a partial exemption.

entries.label: Property tax bill
entries.summary: How to read a NJ tax bill: assessed value, tax rate, deductions, quarterly payments and block and lot.
entries.where: Guides > How to read a NJ tax bill

entries.label: Property tax due dates
entries.summary: NJ property taxes are due quarterly on Feb 1, May 1, Aug 1 and Nov 1. Many towns allow a grace period of up to 10 days.

entries.label: ROBUST Framework

entries.label: Recourse (ROBUST R)
entries.summary: How realistic an appeal looks, based on county appeal history and the strength of the evidence.

entries.label: Overassessment Position (ROBUST O)
entries.summary: Whether a property looks over-assessed, comparing its assessment with supported value and Chapter 123.

entries.label: Burden (ROBUST B)
entries.summary: How heavy the yearly tax is compared with the home's supported market value.

entries.label: Uniformity (ROBUST U)
entries.summary: How evenly a town assesses homes, based on the state coefficient of deviation, and how that feeds the Watchdog Score.

entries.label: Stability (ROBUST S)
entries.summary: How likely assessments are to shift, based on revaluation pressure, ratio drift and town uniformity.

entries.label: Trajectory (ROBUST T)
entries.summary: Where a property's assessment is heading compared with verified sales and town ratios.
